steps.what: Initiate discussions, invite competing interpretations and moderate participation

tasks.design: The lecturer continues live discussion and responds to students' reasoning. The {LMS} may hold materials, but its runtime does not replace moderation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work depends on live participation and interpretation.
tasks.enabler_now: No demonstrated change replaces that interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Encouraging quieter students while challenging unsound legal arguments.
tasks.human_edge: Read the room and make a defensible teaching intervention.
tasks.altitude: Discussion time and teaching authority stay unchanged.

evidence.claim: Live moderation has no established labour replacement in this proposal.

assumptions: Boundary is live discussion; preparation belongs to the materials task.
Student contributions are received directly during s1, without transcription or structured participation scores.
Test existing LMS features before adding tools; no change is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no new system or recording process is introduced.
research_questions: Which discussion difficulties require additional facilitation training?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100; gross and net zero. Both large seminars and small tutorials retain live moderation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select learning outcomes, legal sources and requirements for course materials
Draft syllabi, homework assignments and handouts from the selected brief

loop.purpose: Draft teaching prose from supplied sources
loop.input: Materials brief and quoted source passages
loop.check: Lecturer checks every legal proposition, jurisdiction, date and alignment with learning outcomes
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported propositions return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates arrange headings but cannot adapt legal explanations to the class

steps.what: Check legal accuracy, correct examples and accept final course materials

tasks.design: Use existing {DOCS} templates first, adding a bounded drafting loop only for explanatory prose. The lecturer supplies sources and checks the entire final version; student publication is outside this preparation task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reusable layouts do not draft explanations or examples.
tasks.enabler_now: Source constrained drafting can propose editable teaching text.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting misleading simplifications and outdated legal propositions.
tasks.human_edge: Choose the legal reasoning students must learn.
tasks.altitude: A small amount of drafting time shifts to checking explanations; teaching authority is unchanged.

reach.learn: Assess whether examples test the intended reasoning

evidence.claim: EduGenAI supplies a teaching chat platform; this does not establish legal accuracy or time savings.
The proposed source constrained drafting and effort estimates are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers preparation only, excluding teaching and publication.

Lecturer produces s1 brief: course id, outcomes, audience, jurisdiction, effective date, timetable, assignment requirements and source passages with versions; capture is included in s1. Missing sources require manual writing.
Test native DOCS templates before adding the loop; existing runtime earns no saving.
No student personal information or confidential legal case files are needed.
unknowns: Availability of reusable materials and permitted drafting environment
research_questions: Does checking source supported drafts take less time than writing comparable handouts?

approvals.approved_version: Exact final materials version, source versions and jurisdiction/date; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=89.5; gross10.5 minus5 upkeep gives5.5 net. Novel legal topics may need manual rewriting; repeated handouts may yield2%.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade law examinations

steps.what: Set examination questions, rubric and permitted combinations
Compile examinations from selected items and approved layout rules
Check the examination version, administer it and collect student answers
Grade examinations, resolve ambiguous reasoning and accept results

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} question bank and examination layout from lecturer selected items. The lecturer checks the assembled examination before use and retains administration and legal answer grading.
tasks.previous_blocker: Question selection and repeated document assembly are often interleaved.
tasks.enabler_now: Native item bank configuration can separate assembly from substantive examination design.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing defensible but unexpected legal reasoning.
tasks.human_edge: Set valid questions and decide the marks.
tasks.altitude: Less assembly work; examination and result authority stay with the lecturer.

reach.learn: Version items without exposing examination content

evidence.claim: Ans supports closed question marking and distribution of open questions among markers; this proposal retains legal answer grading.
Configured item assembly savings are a task design estimate, not a measured legal teaching result.

assumptions: Boundary excludes ordinary coursework grading and subsequent result publication.

Lecturer captures item id/version, exact question text, selection order, marks, rubric, permitted combination and layout in s1; this capture time remains. Missing structured fields trigger manual assembly, not inferred rules.
Student registry produces the existing candidate roster; no change or saving is claimed there. Lecturer checks attendance and associates answer ids during s3, with all time retained.
Test native LMS item bank configuration first; no automatic legal grading is assumed.
unknowns: Item bank availability and examination format
research_questions: Can native assembly reproduce approved examination layouts without extra checking?

approvals.approved_version: Exact assembled examination version, questions, order, rubric and marks; any edit requires recheck
Exact candidate answer versions, rubric and final result set; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=85 gross15 minus6 upkeep gives9 net. Already configured exams yield zero additional saving; repeat item assembly may yield3%.

steps.what: Evaluate assignments, papers and oral presentations against the rubric
Write feedback explaining the assessment and ways to improve

loop.purpose: Express instructor judgments as clear feedback
loop.input: Assessment notes with rubric criteria and evidence
loop.check: Lecturer verifies each criticism, suggested improvement and rubric alignment against the work
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unsupported feedback is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Fixed rubric comments may not explain the student's particular legal argument

steps.what: Correct feedback and accept the coursework grade

tasks.design: Use native rubric comments in the {LMS} first, then draft narrative feedback from lecturer notes where needed. The lecturer evaluates the work and accepts every grade and feedback version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing individual feedback repeats part of the assessment reasoning.
tasks.enabler_now: Feedback drafting can work from instructor notes rather than deciding grades.
tasks.still_hard: Evaluating original legal arguments and fair treatment of oral work.
tasks.human_edge: Judge the student's reasoning and decide the result.
tasks.altitude: Small reductions in feedback wording; assessment responsibility stays unchanged.

reach.learn: Distinguish weak legal reasoning from unconventional valid arguments

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes.
Effort assumptions for legal coursework feedback are unmeasured.

assumptions: Boundary covers coursework, excluding the examination task and downstream publication or appeals.

Lecturer produces rubric criterion, work reference, observed strength/weakness, suggested improvement and provisional grade in s1; note capture is included. Oral presentations are observed live and noted in s1 without assumed recordings.
Missing notes or uncertain evidence means manual feedback, never invented evidence or automatic scores.
Test native rubric and comment tools first; use only an approved environment for student information.
unknowns: Existing feedback effort and permitted use of student work
research_questions: Does checking drafted feedback preserve accuracy and reduce total marking time?

already_counted.description: Draft review, correction and grade acceptance

incremental.description: Maintain feedback examples and inspect recurring errors

approvals.approved_version: Exact student work version, rubric, grade and final feedback; changes require renewed acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=92.5 gross7.5 minus4 upkeep gives3.5 net. Complex arguments may need full rewriting; routine feedback may yield1%.
